# Balance and harmony

Source: *The UI/UX Playbook* (uxpeak). Each entry separates **what the PDF states** from **our interpretation of its images**. Text explanations are complete without the images. Back to the [index](../index.md).

<a id="bal-01"></a>
## BAL-01 - Keep proportion and scale so no element overpowers

Each element should have its own space and prominence without one oversized element taking over.

- **Source:** PDF 36 (printed 35), 37 (printed 36)
- **Applies when:** Cards and compositions with an image, text and a CTA.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- Balance and harmony make elements fit together, look good and be easier to understand quickly.
- Proportion and scale: no single element should overpower the others.
- In the incorrect kiwi ice-cream card the image and the large full-width 'Get now' button are too big; the eye doesn't know where to go and crucial details are lost.

**Mistake:** Oversized image and oversized CTA with tiny supporting text.  
**Effect:** Competing focal points; details get lost.

**Correction:** Reduce the image and CTA so the heading, description and rating get readable space.  
**Why it works:** Balanced proportions create a single, calm reading path.

**Observable checks:**
- Do two or more elements each try to be the largest thing in the component?
- Is supporting text so small relative to the hero element that it is overlooked?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Related:** [VH-02](02-visual-hierarchy.md#vh-02), [BAL-02](10-balance.md#bal-02)

<a id="bal-02"></a>
## BAL-02 - Don't overuse a single colour

Using one colour everywhere is monotonous or overwhelming; use complementary or analogous colours for variation and balance.

- **Source:** PDF 36 (printed 35), 37 (printed 36)
- **Applies when:** Colour selection for a component or screen.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- Colour harmony: overusing one colour can be monotonous or overwhelming; complementary or analogous colours add variation and emotional balance.
- The incorrect kiwi card uses green for the image background, the CTA and decorations.

**Mistake:** One saturated hue applied to background, CTA and decorations.  
**Effect:** Monotonous and overwhelming; nothing stands out.

**Correction:** Use a softer complementary background (peach in the source) and keep the brand hue for the CTA.  
**Why it works:** Variation lets the accent colour mean something.

**Observable checks:**
- Is the accent colour used on large background areas as well as on the CTA?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Related:** [COL-01](14-color.md#col-01)

<a id="bal-03"></a>
## BAL-03 - Keep relationships between elements consistent

Consistent spacing, typography and element sizes create harmonious relationships between elements.

- **Source:** PDF 36 (printed 35)
- **Applies when:** All compositions.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- Element relationships: consistent spacing, typography and element sizes create a harmonious relationship.

**Mistake:** Inconsistent spacing, font sizes or element sizes within one composition.  
**Effect:** Disharmony.

**Correction:** Apply shared spacing (WS-03) and type scales.  
**Why it works:** Consistency is perceived as harmony.

**Observable checks:**
- Are similar elements given the same size, type style and spacing?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Source issues / ambiguity:**
- Text-only principle; no dedicated visual example.

**Related:** [WS-03](08-whitespace.md#ws-03), [CNS-01](11-consistency.md#cns-01)
